Subject: Your first order starts here — gear basics, no fluff
CTA: Browse Gear Basics -> https://www.example.com/gear-basics
Body: Hey,

You've spent time out there. You know what a bad night in a poorly rated sleeping bag feels like, and you know the difference between a trail that forgives and one that doesn't.

So this isn't a lecture. It's a short, honest rundown of what to look for when you're buying gear with us for the first time.

---

**Start with the trip, not the gear.**

Before you look at a single product, write down three things: where you're going, how long you'll be out, and what season you're traveling in. Every choice — pack volume, insulation rating, boot height — follows from those answers.

---

**Weight is a real number, not a feeling.**

When a product lists a packed weight, that's the number you carry. Add it to your other items and see what your base weight becomes. Most three-season backpackers aim to keep base weight under 20 lbs. Ultralight setups push under 10 lbs. Know your target before you buy.

---

**Ratings tell you the floor, not the ceiling.**

A sleeping bag rated to 20°F will keep most sleepers functional at 20°F — not warm, functional. If you run cold, size down by 10°F. If you're car camping versus summit camping, that distinction matters more than the brand name on the zipper.

---

**Pack volume is geometry, not ambition.**

A 65-liter pack holds roughly 65 liters of gear. That sounds obvious, but it's easy to buy big and carry too much. A 3-day trip typically fits in 35–50 liters for experienced packers. A 7-day trip in shoulder season may need 55–70 liters. Match the bag to the trip length first.

---

**What we're not going to oversell you.**

No piece of gear here solves bad planning. A 10,000mm waterproof rating keeps you dry in sustained rain — it won't compensate for an exposed ridge in a lightning storm. Boots with a B2 crampons rating are not built for technical alpine ice. We'll always tell you what the gear is built for, and where it stops.

---

Ready to put together your first kit? Browse our gear basics collection and filter by trip type, season, or weight. If you're not sure where to start, our fit guide walks you through it in under five minutes.

See you on the trail.
